intro: Fully funded 36-month doctoral researcher in water engineering and monitoring (PFAROS project on PFAS in hospital wastewater) at the University of Luxembourg. EUR 44,531 gross/year. Rolling review.
description:
About the Position

The University of Luxembourg's Faculty of Science, Technology and Medicine (FSTM) is hiring a doctoral researcher in water engineering and monitoring within the PFAROS project, which focuses on PFAS pollution in hospital wastewater (job reference UOL08545, Kirchberg Campus). The project addresses the detection, monitoring and engineering control of per- and polyfluoroalkyl substances (PFAS).

Your Role

  • Advanced laboratory and analytical work on PFAS in wastewater streams
  • Examine large datasets from environmental monitoring campaigns
  • Develop engineering and monitoring approaches for hospital wastewater treatment
  • Publish and communicate results within the project consortium

Funding and Employment

Employment and financial support
ComponentDetails
PositionFixed-term doctoral researcher contract (full time)
SalaryEUR 44,531 gross per year (full time).
LocationUniversity of Luxembourg (campus per project)
NoteThe University of Luxembourg is a multilingual, international research university.
ContractFixed-term for 36 months, full-time (40 hours/week)
CampusKirchberg Campus, Luxembourg

Eligibility and Requirements

Academic and research preparation
CriterionRequirement
Academic preparationMaster's degree in Chemical Engineering, Materials Engineering, Environmental Engineering, or an equivalent engineering degree.
SkillsAdvanced competence in laboratory and analytical work; capability to examine large data sets.
LanguagesVery good command of English required; good working knowledge of German or French is an asset; at least B2-level proficiency in the language of the thesis.

About University of Luxembourg

University of Luxembourg is a multilingual public research university in Luxembourg. It offers bachelor's, master's and doctoral education across science, technology, law, economics, humanities and social sciences. Its research centres and international academic community support collaboration across disciplines, connecting study with topics such as digital transformation, finance and contemporary society.

Official website: https://www.uni.lu
